stack: React 19 + Vite + TypeScript, GSAP 3 ScrollTrigger (template react-gsap)
firstMessage:
/genjutsu:paint redesign this site

Atelier Grès is a fictional pottery studio, made up for this example. Everything it has to say is already on the page.
mode: conversation (client played by an agent from gres-redesign/client.md)
startingPage: the pottery-firing fixture (examples/pottery-firing/fixture.sh in the genjutsu repo): cream paper ground, Georgia, four bordered boxes. It is the same starting point as the pottery-firing example; here the job is a full redesign.

plugin.note: 4.1.1 candidate with the $1/$2 skill-argument substitution fix

exchangesNote: 9 messages from the client, 9 replies from genjutsu; the client agent's tenth reply was <<DONE>>, which ends the run and is not part of the conversation.
modulesLoadedNote: From the load_skill / load_ref calls and script runs in the session log. The run's own report lists the same six modules and 'Modules not loaded: none'.
previewMode: A (rendered page), standalone HTML files under preview/
visualThesis:
**Visual thesis:** I'm redesigning the whole visual layer. It's one page whose background follows a piece through the kiln:
- the cool grey-buff of bone-dry clay
- the salmon of bisque
- the near-black of a kiln in reduction, where the only light is a soft spy-hole glow
- the grey-green celadon that reduced iron gives a glaze, at the end

Text is iron-black, and the firing measures are in oxidised-iron rust. The display face is still undecided and gets chosen at the design-system step (it won't be Georgia). It should be one face with tabular figures for the temperatures and a big size jump from body text to headline. The layout is airy: every stage gets at least a full screen, on an 8px base. Everything is flat with no borders: no cards, square corners, no shadows.
interactionThesis:
**Interaction thesis:** Slow and patient.
- The background colour follows the scroll position and only changes in the gaps between stages, so it holds still while you read.
- The spy-hole glow rises as the glaze firing reaches the middle of the screen. Over the long cooling stage it fades from yellow-orange to dull red to nothing, so the page waits the way the kiln does.
- Text fades in once with a 16px rise over 700ms, eased with `cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)`, 120ms apart.
- No hover effects, because the page has nothing to click.
- Forbidden: flames, flicker, particles, parallax, pinning or scroll-jacking, bounce, any looping animation.
allowedPatterns: **Allowed patterns:** the spy-hole glow (glaze firing and cooling only), the background colour that follows the scroll, a dark background for the glaze firing and cooling, and the firing measures in rust with tabular figures.
designSystemFace: I'm keeping the system face. I can't fetch or render a Google font in this sandbox, so I couldn't check its tabular figures or show it to you, and the thesis depends on the figures.
webFonts: none. The run tried to fetch a Google font (Bricolage Grotesque) and the request produced no file in the sandbox; it kept the platform system face even after the client said a Google Fonts link was fine. The captures render it as SF Pro (headless Chrome on macOS).
changesFromApprovedPreview: **Two changes from the preview you approved, both to fix contrast:** The colour change moved from the whole screen into 40svh gradient seams in the page, and the spy-hole moved out from behind the text into its own column.
clientPushback: Exchange 2, before any thesis: it should not be warm and earthy just because it is pottery; the colours must come from the clay, the fire, the iron and what reduction does to it; keep every word and fact.
Exchange 4: picked kiln light, but 'keep it soft though, it shouldn't look like flames'.
Exchange 7: said a Google Fonts face with more character was fine; genjutsu kept the system face.
Exchange 9: asked to fix the one problem the audit found (the unused colour token).
No pushback on the theses themselves: both were approved on first showing (exchange 6).

captureNotes: Captured with bin/record.mjs: static builds served from disk over CDP, no server, virtual time. Takes are in takes/.

clip.webp and before.webp: the recorder's own encoder could only fit the 12.8 s scroll under 700 KB at 864 px or at 8 fps, and its frame-differencing left faint ghosts of the previous frame's text below each paragraph. The frames were re-encoded from the same take with takes/encode-keyframes.py (Pillow, every frame a keyframe, quality 35 at 10 fps for clip.webp, quality 50 at 12 fps for before.webp). The first 3 and last 4 frames of the 12 fps capture (still frames of the holds at each end) were dropped. No pixel of the page was changed.
No console errors, uncaught exceptions or failed requests in any take.
Checked beyond the run's own handed-over list: no horizontal scroll at 390 and 768 px; jumping straight to the bottom and back reveals every text block (none stays hidden).

Towards the end of cooling the ember has faded to nothing and the screen is plain kiln-dark until the seam into celadon rises from the bottom (visible near the end of clip.webp). That is the thesis ('a long wait before it opens'), not a rendering gap.

Gallery reframe (after the first capture pass): reduced.png retaken at y=3020 so the whole glaze block fits; clip-gallery.webp and before-glaze.png added; mid-glaze.png and mobile-glaze.png picked for the gallery. The build and the run's output were not touched.

clip-gallery.webp: takes/clip-gallery.json is written by takes/make-clip-gallery.mjs, which turns a speed profile into one scroll step per frame (the recorder's eases are per segment, so a profile that slows on the seams is sampled frame by frame). Layout measured with takes/probe-layout.json. Recorded at 12 fps, then encoded with takes/encode-keyframes.py at quality 50, 12 fps. The take jumps to y 2300 and waits 3 s first; the first 35 frames (the jump and the bisque text revealing after it) were dropped at encode, keeping a 0.5 s hold once the reveal is done. In the clip the glaze paragraph reveals a moment after its title as it enters, which is the page's own reveal.
before-glaze.png: takes/before-glaze.json, the fixture build scrolled to y=1076.

defectsIntroduced.what: In both preview pages the spy-hole glow is drawn behind the glaze-firing text, so the light text on the glow is close to unreadable (the run itself measured about 1.3:1 when it later built the page). The client agent approved the theses on this preview without remarking on it.
defectsIntroduced.status: Caught by the run while building: the build puts the glow in its own column, and the run said so in exchange 7. The previews were left as they were and the run flagged them as stale.

defectsIntroduced.what: The report overstates token coverage: it says no one-off numbers are left in the styles and every size comes from a token, but src/index.css still has three literal sizes: `max-width: 13ch` (line 112), `max-width: 40ch` (line 136) and `30svh` inside the cooling padding (line 190).
defectsIntroduced.status: Not reported by the run. Cosmetic; it changes nothing on screen.
